gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours of full sun a kit's own panel needs to refill its battery: 2,048 Wh ÷ 400 W = 5.1 h for the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 + 400 W bundle ChatGPT showed, against 10.4 h for a 2,080 Wh BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 with one 200 W panel and 3.0 h with two 350 W panels.
standout_why: I opened californiabalconysolar.com/sb-868 (cited), the KQED article from 2026-09-30 (cited) and pluginsolartracker.com/california (cited) and checked their figures. All three give only the 1,200 W per-dwelling AC cap and the dates. KQED adds a $300–$2,200 kit price range and claims of 'up to 20%' of a home's electricity and '$500 annually' in savings. None of them names a battery capacity, a panel size, a refill time or a cost per Wh, and none names a product.
decides: Refill hours separate kits that look alike. The Anker C2000 Gen 2 + 400 W bundle ChatGPT showed and a BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 with 2× 200 W panels both need about 5 h of full rated sun to refill, which most balcony days won't give. Each also leaves half or more of its solar input unused (400 of 800 W; 400 of 1,000 W). Of the bundles I priced, only the Elite 200 V2 + 2× 350 W refills in about 3 h, at $1.03/Wh. The single 200 W bundle has the best kit price per Wh ($0.58) but needs 10.4 h, so it can't refill in one day. This favours bundles with at least 700 W of panel when a full daily refill is the goal.
